newsitem.title: LEBANON: LEBANON ISSUES MONEY SUPPLY STATISTICS.
newsitem.headline: LEBANON ISSUES MONEY SUPPLY STATISTICS.

text.p: Lebanon's M1 money stock rose 35.4 billion Lebanese pounds in August to 1,771.4 billion pounds, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly report on Monday.
Its annual growth recorded 24.73 percent relative to August 1995.
M2 rose 267 billion pounds in August registering a 43.24 percent growth over the same month last year, the Bank said.
M3 rose by 343.9 billion pounds in August registering a 1.33 percent monthly increase and a 18.74 percent growth over the same month last year, the Bank added.
M4, a newly-introduced indicator, rose by 613 billion pounds to 30,309 billion pounds, registering a 25.44 percent annual increase.
The Bank issued the following statistics (blns of Lebanese pounds at end of period):
The Bank defined the aggregates as follows:
M1 -- Currency in circulation + Demand deposits
M2 -- M1 + Other deposits in Lebanese pounds
M4 -- M3 + Treasury bills held by the non-banking system
